newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sees fall in corn imports on good supply.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sees fall in corn imports on good supply.

text.p: Indonesian imports of corn should decline in the short term given ample stocks and generally stable demand, traders said on Tuesday.
"I think there will be enough corn in the next couple of months because of the ample supply. We are going to see a decline in corn imports," said one trader.
"There is also some talk about import duty on corn, but this has been sent to the background for the time being. I don't think there's going to be import duty on corn," he added.

Traders said last week Indonesia was flush with corn, with an importer diverting one shipment of 60,000 tonnes to Thailand while another 120,000 tonnes were cancelled because of a lack of storage space.
Traders said demand for corn was generally stable and that it was at quoted at 380-85 rupiah/kg in Jakarta. They said soymeal was quoted at 900 rupiah/kg, unchanged since last week.
"I think corn is sort of weak, because of there is much supply around, but I think soymeal is steady to a little bit firmer," said one trader.
"I think that demand for soymeal is going up in the next couple of months," he added.
One trader said Chinese corn was being offered at $135-$142 a tonne C&F. They said South American soymeal was being offered at $290-294 a tonne C&F, down from $305 last week.
"You know that in South America, the new crops are pushing prices down. Any rallies would be short-lived," said one trader.
Another trader said demand for soymeal from feedmills continued to be high.
"Feedmills continue to work and I learn there will be more ships coming in this month," he said without giving other details.
